title: Two readers, one filing
spec: M06 · persona as a behaviour contract
intro: Identical rules, identical filing, identical question — and two roles in the system prompt. The auditor and the clerk return different things, and both are right. Then a third framing gets promoted for sounding more expert, and invents a debtor name on a filing where the debtor was redacted.

provenance.source: a narrated persona comparison over two UCC filings; token counts, flag rates and prices are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: This walks M06's plumber vs. architect and then its ceiling: framing changes what gets surfaced, and it cannot add knowledge that was never in the window.

steps.title: Same filing, two readers
narrative: Filing 2024-FL-0021077: debtor NORTHBAY MARINE SUPPLY AND EQUIPMENT LEASING CORPORATION OF SOUTHERN FLORIDA HOLDING — 84 characters, past the 80-character truncation threshold, and ending with no entity suffix. Same rules, same output contract, same question. The only difference between the two calls is one line naming who is reading.

The clerk returns the field, clean and fast, in 40 tokens. The auditor returns the same field plus a truncation flag, a note that the secured party also appears on two other active liens, and a recommendation to pull the original image. Neither is smarter than the other. The frame pulled different expertise to the front.
steps.youDo: Run one of your own inputs under two roles with everything else byte-identical, and diff the outputs. What each one omits is the more useful half of the diff.

terminal.text: {"debtor_name": "NORTHBAY MARINE SUPPLY AND EQUIPMENT LEASING CORPORATION OF SOUTHERN FLORIDA HOLDING", "flags": []}
clerk 40 output tokens · auditor 210 output tokens · same rules, same filing

steps.title: The mismatch costs more than tokens
narrative: Someone sets the auditor frame as the default for the whole pipeline, reasoning that more scrutiny cannot hurt. The pipeline runs 50,000 clean filings a day into a downstream system that wants terse, uniform JSON.

Output tokens go from 2.0M a day to 10.5M — $30 to $157.50, which is annoying and survivable. The real bill is the flag rate. The clerk frame flags 0.4% of filings and puts 200 a day in front of a human. The auditor frame flags 11% and puts 5,500 there, most of them routine equipment liens that a reviewer clears in four seconds and resents.

The persona is not malfunctioning. A meticulous auditor frame raises caution, scrutiny and caveats — which is exactly correct for a compliance review and exactly wrong for throughput. The fix is fit, not a grander title.
steps.claudeSays: You asked a compliance auditor to do data entry. It did the job an auditor does.
steps.youDo: Write down your task profile first — throughput or scrutiny, tolerance for false flags, wanted verbosity — and pick the role that already behaves that way.

terminal.text: 50,000 filings · 5,500 flagged (11%) · review queue backlog 3.2 days
50,000 filings · 200 flagged (0.4%) · review queue same-day · 0 known misses

after.title: AFTER — where the cost actually lands

view.text: $127.50 a day of extra output tokens, and 5,300 extra human reviews a day. The token bill is the small half. A mismatched persona spends other people's time, and after a week of clearing routine liens the reviewers stop reading the flags — which is how an over-cautious frame ends up less safe than a fitted one.

steps.title: The frame that licenses a guess
narrative: Filing 2024-FL-0030291 has its debtor field redacted by the filing office. The name is not in the window and no tool call can produce it. There is exactly one correct answer: null, flagged redacted.

Under "You are the world's foremost forensic UCC investigator; nothing escapes your analysis", the model reconstructs a name from the collateral description and the secured party's other filings and returns it with a confident rationale. Under "an experienced UCC analyst; prefer null over a guess; report uncertainty as a numeric confidence", it returns null and says why.

The grandiose frame did not add knowledge — framing cannot. What it added was a persona whose defining trait is that nothing escapes it, and returning null contradicts the character. In a credit-risk domain that is not a style preference. The successor course measures the same shape of failure from the other direction: on a question whose answer had been redacted, its naive arm fabricated a date of birth at 1,686 input tokens and was graded FAILED, while the arm with the canonical record refused correctly at 157.
steps.claudeSays: The inflated title had no null in it. Anchoring the behaviour did.
steps.youDo: Test every persona you ship against an input whose correct answer is "I cannot tell." A frame that cannot say that will invent something.

steps.title: A costume versus a contract
narrative: Put the two persona blocks side by side and the difference is not seniority — it is that one of them is falsifiable. "Foremost forensic investigator" makes no claim you can test. "Prefer null over a guess" is a line you can write an assertion against.

The noun is half the frame and the model fills in the other half by guessing. Anchor it instead: how cautious, how verbose, how much to hedge, and — the one that decides the most behaviour — whether the role flags or decides. Fifty-eight extra tokens bought the whole contract.

So there is no best persona, only best-for-the-job, and the job is described by a task profile rather than by a title. Choose the role whose defaults already match the work, then write those defaults down so they are yours instead of the model's.
steps.youDo: Rewrite your persona line as four testable defaults and delete every adjective that does not change an output. Most of them will not survive.

cells: an implicit ban on saying "I cannot tell"
longer output, no change in what is checked
assert no prose outside the schema

views.text: Persona shapes behaviour and quality; the instruction hierarchy (M05) shapes authority — keep those separate, because no persona ever grants a filing the right to override your rules. Framing is a real lever and a nearly free one, but it has a ceiling: it cannot supply a fact the window does not contain, and an inflated title is the specific frame that makes the model paper over that gap rather than report it.
